text: This lesson is the first real PySpark of the redesign: the incremental Bronze ingestion itself. Four steps -- read the watermark, filter the source to only what's new, append to Bronze, and advance the watermark -- and each one has to happen in exactly that order for the whole thing to be safe.

Step one, read the watermark. meta-dot-last-ingested-date holds one row per source, with the latest date that source has already had ingested. You look it up, filtering on the source name, and if there's no row yet -- the very first run against this source -- you fall back to a date far in the past, so everything available counts as new. That's correct, because nothing has actually been ingested before.

Step two, filter the source files down to only what's new. The source data lands as daily files partitioned by sale date, so the read just adds one filter: sale date greater than the watermark. Notice what this is NOT doing -- it never scans or touches data at or before the watermark. That one filter is the whole point. It's the line that turns reprocess-everything into process-only-what's-new.

Step three, append to Bronze. Add the bookkeeping columns -- source file and ingested-at timestamp -- and write with format delta, mode append, into bronze-dot-sales-raw. Append is the correct mode here specifically because the filter in step two already guaranteed these rows are new. Bronze stays append-only exactly like the Beginner project; the only real change is that far fewer rows show up at this write call each night.

Step four, advance the watermark -- but only after the append has actually succeeded. This matters: advancing it too early, before confirming the write landed, risks silently skipping real data if the run fails partway through. The advance itself is a small merge-into against meta-dot-last-ingested-date -- insert the source if it's new, update its date if it's already there. If no new rows were found at all, the watermark is simply left alone.

That's incremental Bronze ingestion, built end to end: a watermark read, a filter that skips everything already processed, an append of just the new rows, and a watermark advance that only happens after success. Next lesson takes those newly-ingested Bronze rows and merges them into silver-dot-sales-clean, using Delta Lake's real merge-into for the first time against the full sales data.
